newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana Aluworks share offer only 49 pct subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Aluworks share offer only 49 pct subscribed.

text.p: Investors showing caution ahead of Ghanaian elections next month, largely ignored a share offer by Ghana's Aluworks Ltd, West Africa's leading aluminium rolling mill, brokers said on Wednesday.
The offer of five million Aluworks ordinary shares was undersubscribed by 51 percent, the brokers told Reuters.
Only about 2.4 million shares were subscribed and fully paid for by 140 investors, said co-manager Databank Brokerage Ltd.
Priced at 1,350 cedis per share, Aluworks raised about 3.3 billion cedis ($1.93 million) instead of the targeted 6.75 billion cedis.

"It has been a bear. But in fact, I am amazed that we managed to sell as many as this, considering that we came out this late in the year and in a pre-election period," Databank director Kelyi Gadzekpo told Reuters.
Ghana holds presidential and parliamentary elections on December 7.

"Anyway, the primary reason for the offer was not to raise money but to get listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange. As we exceeded the minimum (two billion cedis) that target has been reached," Gadzekpo said.
"We expected more from foreign institutions as Aluworks is a very solid investment. But due to the elections there is this wait-and see attitude", he added.

The Commonwealth Development Corp, the French agency Caisse Francaise de Developpement and the World Bank's private sector investment arm International Finance Corp have indicated that they will come in later, according to Gadzekpo.
Apart from the current issue, six million shares had been reserved since May for a period of two years for these institutional investors, he said.
A total of 102 individual entities in Ghana bought almost 220,000 shares worth about 296 million cedis. Five non-resident individuals paid a total of $7,400 for 9,250 shares.
Four foreign corporates, all emerging market funds -- one each from Switzerland and the UK and two from the United States -- obtained a total of 780,000 shares worth almost $607,000.
With annual capacity of 20,000 tonnes, Aluworks is the largest aluminium rolling mill outside of South Africa and one of the six aluminium rolling mills in Africa.
It is scheduled to enter the Ghana Stock Exchange on Friday as the bourse's 21st listing.
Following the share offer the government's stake in Aluworks has been reduced to 36.70 percent from 45.32 percent.
Other main shareholders are the Ghana Social Security Bank, with 14.2 percent, and cocoa marketing authority Cocobod, with 10.25 percent.
